coachingReview.label: Sourced reading of the match reports. Not a model, and not a film review. No footage was watched for this card.
coachingReview.coverage: One Test, from articles and the live blog fetched on 8 Nov 2026. A full penalty count, a kick map, and metres gained are not in those pages. Where a report disagrees with another, both are shown.

items.title: Scotland scored from a driven line-out
items.confidence: Named in more than one report
items.evidence: Ewan Ashman's first try, about 8 minutes, is a rolling maul in the Scottish Rugby report and 'patience at the maul' on the live blog, after Kyle Rowe's 50:22. BBC calls it a driven line-out. Ashman's second, about 26 minutes, is not a maul: BBC says he blasted through Wallace Sititi off a penalty advantage. Ashman's third, about 37 minutes, is a line-out maul in the BBC report. The Scottish Rugby report does not use the word maul for that third try.
items.reading: One Scotland try is a rolling or driven maul on every report that describes it. A second maul try is BBC only. This is one match, not a season trend.
items.response: Stop the first drive while staying on feet. Collapsing a maul is not the action.
items.practice: Coaching suggestion, tied to the scored maul: two defenders, the first on the ball carrier and the second on the drive, both bound and on their feet. World Rugby's law list includes Law 16, Maul. The page did not load the law text, so no subsection is quoted.
items.measure: Proposed count, not a figure from this match: opposition line-out drives that move more than a few metres or score. Murrayfield has no such count in this file.

items.title: New Zealand also scored from the line-out
items.confidence: Named in more than one report
items.evidence: Codie Taylor, about 19 or 20 minutes: BBC says a Scotland penalty was kicked and the All Blacks scored from the line-out maul. The All Blacks report says a line-out drive at 19 minutes. The live blog says the penalty count against Scotland was mounting and Taylor dotted down. Wallace Sititi, about 3 or 4 minutes, is not a maul: the live blog says a kick to touch after a Scotland offside, then a corner score; BBC says dummy runners at a close-range line-out.
items.reading: The Taylor score is a penalty kick to touch, then a drive or maul. The Sititi score is a planned line-out, not a rolling maul. Both are New Zealand attacks, not a failure to maul.
items.response: Keep the penalty-to-touch call when the side is inside the opposition 22. Do not treat it as the same skill as stopping Scotland's maul.
items.practice: Coaching suggestion: from a penalty inside the 22, the kicker and the line-out caller name touch or tap before the kick. That habit is not something these reports measured.
items.measure: Proposed count, not a Murrayfield stat: penalties kicked to the corner that end in a retained drive or a score.

items.title: Ethan de Groot's try is not a settled mechanism
items.confidence: Do not coach off one version
items.evidence: About 15 or 16 minutes, after Matt Fagerson was penalised. The live blog says a quickly taken tap and de Groot powered through. BBC says New Zealand went to touch and de Groot went over. The Scottish report says he barged over and does not say tap or line-out.
items.reading: It is a try from a Scotland penalty. It is not established as a maul, a tap, or a kick to the corner.
items.response: Leave it out of the maul plan and out of the kicking plan.
items.practice: No drill is attached. A drill would pick a version the sources do not share.
items.measure: None. A mechanism count would invent the method.

items.title: Two New Zealand yellow cards, and no verified penalty total
items.status: Observed cards. The count is incomplete
items.confidence: Cards are named. The totals are not
items.evidence: Peter Lakai was shown yellow for a run of offsides. BBC, the live blog and the Scottish report agree. Ashman's second try came while Lakai was off, on BBC's account. Wallace Sititi was shown yellow as Lakai returned. BBC says Sititi went off his feet. The Scottish report says a team accumulation of infringements. Ashman's third followed. BBC says those cards cost 14 points, which is the two converted tries, not a separate official table. Sione Tuipulotu, Scotland's captain, was shown yellow for repeated team infringements. Beauden Barrett's second try followed. Before Taylor's try the Scottish report says the penalty count was 5-0 against Scotland. Later the same report says New Zealand had surpassed Scotland's penalty count, with no number. The All Blacks report says, with Scotland as the subject, that they conceded 13 to eight. That 13-8 figure is not in the other reports.
items.reading: The first-half cards are a discipline event in this match. A season trend is not established here. A final penalty count is not cross-checked, so 13-8 is not used as the match total.
items.response: The named offences are offside in one phase, and either off feet or a team tally for Sititi. The next step is to record the offence, not to treat the side as ill-disciplined from the score.
items.practice: Coaching suggestion: in opposed sessions, stop the rep when the whistle is offside or off feet, and restart only after the call is named. This does not use a Murrayfield penalty total.
items.measure: Proposed count for the next Test: penalties and cards in each half, split by offside, off feet, scrum and other. Write it during the match. It is not a stat from Murrayfield.

items.title: Kicking depth is not shown
items.confidence: Do not treat a hypothesis as a finding
items.evidence: No report gives a New Zealand kick count, a share of contestable kicks, or a depth. The kicks that are described are a penalty kick to touch before Sititi's try, Kyle Rowe's 50:22 for Scotland, and Josh Moorby's cover on a Scotland grubber at the end of the half. Damian McKenzie kicked 4 conversions from 7 tries. The live blog says he had missed the attempt before converting Beauden Barrett's second. That is a place-kick, not a territorial kick.
items.reading: Aimless kicking, or kicking too deep, is not established. Saying it from the score would be a guess.
items.response: No kicking-fault plan comes from this match.
items.practice: Generic preparation only, not an observed fault: each kick has a named purpose, touch, contest or territory, and a named chaser. Do not brief it as something Murrayfield proved.
items.measure: Proposed count, not a Murrayfield stat: kicks with a called purpose and a chaser who arrived. It was not recorded here.

items.title: The second half was 19 points to nil
items.confidence: The split is in the scores. The cause is not
items.evidence: Half-time was Scotland 21, New Zealand 24, on the live blog and the All Blacks scoring summary. Full-time was 21-43. Scotland did not score after the break. New Zealand added 19. BBC says 19-0 in the second half. Josh Moorby scored from scrum pressure, about 48 minutes: the report says the third scrum, and the live blog says they scrummed a penalty inside the five metres. Barrett's second, about 50 or 51 minutes, came after Tuipulotu's yellow. Asafo Aumua's try, about 67 minutes, is a set-piece score in the BBC report. It does not say maul.
items.reading: The reports call the second half one-way. The scoreline agrees. That does not identify maul defence or kicking as the cause.
items.response: For Cardiff, these are preparation priorities, not a verified Wales weakness. Nothing in these reports scouts Wales.
items.practice: Order for the week: legal maul stop first, then the penalty-to-corner call, then a live penalty-and-card tally. Kicking purpose stays a generic habit, labelled as not shown in this match.
items.measure: Proposed for Wales, not a result: drives stopped, penalties kicked to touch that are retained, and cards by offence. Collect them on the day.

plan: First: legal stop of the first drive. Scotland's opening try was a rolling maul. Do not collapse it.
Second: keep the penalty kick to touch that led to Taylor's drive. That is an attack, separate from the maul stop.
Third: log offside and off-feet whistles. Two yellow cards are described. A full penalty total is not.
Not in the plan as a fault: kicking too deep or without a chase. The reports do not show it.

southAfrica.title: South Africa
facts: The four-Test series is finished. South Africa won it 3–1. Nothing in this series is live.

New Zealand won the first Test 33–16 at Emirates Airline Park on 22 August (ESPN calls that ground Ellis Park, Johannesburg), then lost 26–33 at Cape Town Stadium on 29 August (ESPN says DHL Stadium, Cape Town), 24–29 at First National Bank Stadium on 5 September (ESPN says FNB Stadium, Johannesburg), and 28–43 at M&T Bank Stadium in Baltimore on 12 September. The scores are the same on Rugby Database and ESPN.
Codie Taylor captained the Baltimore Test. Ardie Savea had already gone home with a dislocated shoulder.

australia.title: Australia
australia.meta: Bledisloe Cup · Eden Park and Sydney played
facts: Saturday 10 October, Eden Park: New Zealand won 50–19. Half-time was 17–14. Rugby Database crowd 46,352. Kick-off 7.10pm New Zealand time.
Saturday 17 October, Accor Stadium: Australia 21, New Zealand 43. Rugby Database game 30266, crowd 73,399, kick-off 3:45pm. The ESPN results list and Sky Sports show the same final score.

New Zealand tries at Sydney: Josh Moorby 2, Beauden Barrett 2, Peter Lakai, Rieko Ioane, Wallace Sititi. Damian McKenzie kicked four conversions and no penalties. Australia tries: Jeremy Williams, Tom Wright, Filipo Daugunu. Ryan Lonergan kicked two conversions and Declan Meredith one. Rugby Database lists no penalty tries.
Half-time is not on the Rugby Database game page. A Rugby Australia report says 36–7 at the break. Sky Sports lists try minutes that do not add to 36 before half-time, so no half-time is shown.

The cup was retained at Eden Park. allblacks.com says New Zealand have held it since 2003. BBC says a 23rd straight year. Sky and an ESPN story say a 24th year. This page does not pick a year count. Rugby Australia's Sydney report calls the result a clean sweep.
The Sydney match-day 23 is the Rugby Database game page. It does not name a captain.

On 11 October the All Blacks said Leroy Carter, Asafo Aumua, Anton Segner and Ethan Blackadder would not travel to Sydney. That note is still the injury source. The Sydney game page does not say whether they have returned.

gamePlan.heading: All Blacks game plan (public reporting)
gamePlan.label: Compiled from public reporting. The South Africa notes were collected on 28 Sep 2026. The Eden Park notes were added on 12 Oct 2026. The Scotland preparation note was added on 8 Nov 2026 from the match reports. This is not AI analysis, and it is not an internal All Blacks document.

bullets.text: New Zealand led 17–14 at half-time and won 50–19. Five tries came after the break. On 1News, Dave Rennie said a quality performance was coming, that the first half was an arm wrestle, and that a few opportunities were left out there. He said Cam Roigard's kicking was excellent, that they kicked more off nine than they had been, and that the side won kicks in the air or picked up the scraps. He said areas that needed to be better after South Africa showed shifts. An ESPN story quoted him crediting mindset, work rate and brutality, and saying the Wallabies would be hurting. The same story quoted Les Kiss saying New Zealand won the aerial battle and that Roigard's kicking was pinpoint.

The All Blacks site, reviewing the South Africa series, said the attack can trouble the Springboks, but that New Zealand too often needed long passages of possession to score. ESPN's Liam Napier wrote on 20 Sep 2026 that Dave Rennie and Mike Blair have aimed the attack at pace and at space out wide, and he reported 35 tries in seven Tests. The score sheets added up to 35 tries at that date. With the Eden Park Test they add up to 42.

After the Baltimore loss, Rennie said the high ball put the side under more heat and that they could not take a lot of those balls. The All Blacks site listed collection of contested kicks as a review area. ESPN reported that the high ball is still a problem and gave Will Jordan a series-high 24 turnovers. That turnover figure is ESPN's count. It is not an official All Blacks statistic re-counted here.

Rennie said the scrum and lineout in the Baltimore Test were excellent. Across the series, ESPN reported 14 scrum penalties conceded, including one penalty try, and a lineout at 86 percent after eight lost throws. Those series figures are ESPN's. The All Blacks site named set-piece consistency as a review area. The penalty try in the score sheets is the Soweto one, awarded to South Africa.

Rennie said needless penalties have to come out of the game, and he called that sort of penalty dumb. The All Blacks site said South Africa were more ruthless after penalties and turnovers. ESPN wrote that smaller wingers stationed in midfield, Leroy Carter and Josh Moorby, were pushed off the ball and that this led to three tries.

Rennie said he was happy with Beauden Barrett off the bench in Baltimore, and that the side has cover at first-five and fullback in Richie Mo'unga, Ruben Love, Damian McKenzie and Beauden Barrett. He also praised Kyle Preston's speed to the breakdown. He said the Bledisloe group would be a squad of 34, with Luke Jacobson and Ardie Savea out, and with Scott Barrett and Leicester Fainga'anuku among those expected back.

The side won its first four Tests, including 33–16 at Ellis Park, then lost the next three. South Africa won the series 3–1. Rennie said the tour was meant to teach them about their game model, that the Baltimore result hurts, and that he still feels they are tracking in the right direction while needing to be better against a side like the Springboks. On 10 October they won 50–19 against Australia at Eden Park. Half-time was 17–14, and five of the seven New Zealand tries came after the break.

bullets.topic: What Rennie said he wanted, before July
bullets.text: Before the July Tests, Rennie told Sky Sport NZ, as reported by SABC Sport, that he treats counter-attack as a set piece because so much possession arrives from kicks, and that he wanted more tries from counter-attack and turnover ball than the year before. The 2025 split he mentioned is his recollection. It is not re-counted here.

These are preparation priorities from the Murrayfield reports. They are not a verified Wales weakness. Scotland's first try was a rolling maul, about 8 minutes. Codie Taylor's try, about 19 minutes, was a New Zealand line-out drive after a Scotland penalty. Peter Lakai and Wallace Sititi were shown yellow in the first half. A final penalty count is not cross-checked, and no report shows aimless or overly deep New Zealand kicking. The detailed card is on the Scotland post-match. Cardiff uses the same priorities as practice, not as a scouted exploit.

How many years the Bledisloe Cup has been held. allblacks.com says since 2003. BBC says a 23rd straight year. Sky and ESPN say a 24th year. No count is shown.
Leroy Carter's return date. RNZ said a high ankle sprain, a likely long spell out, and that the November Tests in Britain are in doubt. No calendar day.
Whether Fehi Fineanganofo travelled to Sydney. He was unavailable at Eden Park with concussion and a hamstring. The 11 October list of four players staying home does not name him.
Richie Mo'unga's return date. A calf strain kept him out of Eden Park. The All Blacks selection story said he is likely to miss Sydney. No calendar day.
Ethan Blackadder's return date. A calf injury in the Eden Park warm-up keeps him out of Sydney. RNZ said it is not thought to be serious. No calendar day.
Asafo Aumua and Anton Segner's return dates. Both failed a second head-injury assessment. The stand-down is a minimum of 12 days. No calendar day was published.

Scott Barrett's minutes at Eden Park. He started, left the field, failed a head-injury assessment that night, then passed a second assessment and travelled. The minute he left is not on the score sheet.
Will Jordan's career try total. 1News said the Eden Park try moved his tally to 56. That is not re-counted here. The Test sheets in this file give him 11 tries.
Tackle counts in the 1News report: Jordie Barrett 16 tackles, Australia 200 tackles, New Zealand 144. Reported, not re-counted here.
Ardie Savea's exact return date. On 4 October Dave Rennie said Savea will not be back until Super Rugby in 2027, and he is not sure that will be in time for the start. There is no calendar day.
ESPN's series counts from Liam Napier's review: 14 scrum penalties, a lineout at 86 percent, eight lost lineouts, and 24 high-ball turnovers for Will Jordan. Reported, not re-counted here.
Nations Championship Finals Weekend, 27–29 November in London. The opponent is not known, so it is not a fixture.
Try scorers for the four tour matches. Rugby Database's games list has the score, venue and crowd. It does not list tries. They are left blank.
